text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Bundestag debates stability and jobs before Dublin summit
- No agreement over reform of public service law
- More than 90 Lufthansa flights cancelled due to strike
- BDA president Hundt asks for total change of course
- Bundestag approves 1997 tax law
- In east 456,000 flats standing empty
HANDELSBLATT
- Germany loses importance as a location for Siemens
- Herzog criticises employers
- Strike at Lufthansa -- 92 flights cancelled
- SPD makes EU policies election campaign theme
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Government looks for new confrontation with SPD
- Lufthansa flights hit by strike
- Beckenbauer has no chance for FIFA president's job
- New employers' president practices fierce criticism of government
- Power firms join forces
- Euro banknotes defy the superstitious
DIE WELT
- Bundestag says yes to currency union
- Herzog reasons with employers
- Way is clear for passing of 1997 tax bill
- Lufthansa strikes cost millions, 92 flights cancelled
- Zwickel sees victory for union
- Greenpeace capture ship carrying gene maize -- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 26097160
